title: A Computational Systems Model of Multi-Level Governance for Human Flourishing Under Bounded Non-Exploitation
content: Governance operates simultaneously across multiple levels—from local communities to national governments to international institutions—yet most formal governance models treat governance as a single-level phenomenon and permit jurisdictions to advance their own flourishing at the expense of others. This conceptual paper extends the General Governance Success Model (GSM) to account for multi-level governance under a bounded non-exploitation constraint: no jurisdiction may impose uncompensated, non-trivial sacrifices on other jurisdictions for its own benefit. The extended model represents governance at L levels, each characterized by five coupled capabilities (accountability, institutional competence, social cohesion, strategic continuity, and adaptive learning). The framework formalizes vertical and horizontal interactions decomposed into cooperative and exploitative components, cross-level information flows with fidelity matrices, level-specific dynamics, recursive learning, and a formal non-exploitation constraint that admits both threshold tolerance and compensation as legitimate exceptions. A formal welfare function is specified, and the threshold parameter τj is decomposed into descriptive contextual variables and normative parameters. Compensation is modelled as a vector of transfers (fiscal, infrastructural, representational, regulatory, and future-oriented). A roadmap for operationalizing the exploitation index is provided. The model generates testable hypotheses concerning vertical alignment, polycentric governance, cross-level coordination, recursive learning, and non-exploitation. An illustrative worked example applying the GSM to Denmark—using real raw governance indicators but explicitly illustrative coefficients—is presented for pedagogical purposes, with comparative rankings relegated to a brief supplementary illustration. To support replication and application, the model is released as an open-source Python library, gsm-governance, which implements the state-space dynamics, bounded non-exploitation constraint, vector-valued compensation, threshold decomposition, and all reported indices. The extended GSM provides a foundation for analysing governance systems in their full institutional complexity while respecting normative constraints on inter-jurisdictional justice.
